nodes.label: SEVERANCE — Lumon Industries (scroll-driven site)
nodes.rationale: An immersive scroll-driven journey down to the severed floor: eight chapters, one continuous camera, no page reloads. Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript only so the whole piece is a single scroll timeline. Fan work with no assets from the show — every mark is drawn in code and every photograph rendered for this build.

nodes.label: Single continuous scroll timeline
nodes.rationale: Eight chapters share one camera and one scroll timeline with no page reloads, so the narrative reads as one continuous descent rather than a sequence of pages.

nodes.label: ES modules + import map (no dev build step)
nodes.rationale: The site uses ES modules and an import map so it must be served over HTTP; opening index.html from the filesystem will not work. In development nothing is compiled — what you edit is what the browser runs — which removes the build step from the authoring loop.
nodes.norm_label: es modules + import map (no dev build step)

nodes.label: Development static server (npm start, tools/serve.mjs)
nodes.rationale: npm start serves on http://localhost:4173; any static server works equally well because there is no bundler in development.

nodes.label: Production build (npm run build → dist/)
nodes.rationale: dist/ is a self-contained folder that can be dropped on any static host with no server configuration and no runtime CDN dependency. The build deliberately only does the things a static host cannot: bundling, concatenation, vendoring and content hashing. Total is about 208 kB gzipped, fonts aside.

nodes.label: Single tree-shaken JS bundle
nodes.rationale: Modules are bundled and minified and Three.js is tree-shaken down to the classes the stage actually touches: 1.2 MB of ESM becomes a 538 kB bundle, 140 kB over the wire.

nodes.label: Single concatenated stylesheet
nodes.rationale: The four sheets are concatenated in cascade order and minified to 37 kB / 8.7 kB gzipped; cascade order must be preserved because the sheets depend on it.

nodes.label: Vendored libraries in dist/vendor/
nodes.rationale: GSAP, ScrollTrigger, CustomEase and Lenis are downloaded into dist/vendor/ at build time so a deploy cannot drift when a CDN changes what it serves. The --no-vendor flag keeps the original CDN script tags instead, which is preferable when sharing the browser's cached copy of GSAP with other sites matters more than deploy determinism.

nodes.label: Content-hashed asset filenames
nodes.rationale: app-<hash>.js / app-<hash>.css let a host cache assets forever and still ship updates.

nodes.label: Built HTML keeps its indentation
nodes.rationale: Authoring comments are stripped and the import map disappears (Three.js is inside the bundle), but markup indentation is kept: collapsing it risks changing significant whitespace and gzip flattens the size difference anyway.

nodes.label: --no-vendor build flag
nodes.rationale: Keeps the original CDN <script> tags rather than vendoring, trading deploy determinism for a shared browser cache of GSAP.

nodes.label: --sourcemap build flag
nodes.rationale: Emits a source map next to the bundle.

nodes.label: GSAP 3
nodes.rationale: Drives every timeline, pin and scrubbed animation; its ticker is also the single RAF loop for the whole site.

nodes.label: GSAP ScrollTrigger
nodes.rationale: Provides pinning and scrubbing; its onRefresh callback is the only place layout measurements are taken.

nodes.label: CustomEase 'lumon' curve
nodes.rationale: A single named easing curve used for institutional motion, giving the whole piece a consistent corporate cadence.

nodes.label: Lenis smooth scrolling
nodes.rationale: Smooth scrolling driven from GSAP's ticker with its own RAF disabled, so scroll and animation share one loop.

nodes.label: Three.js r180 WebGL stage
nodes.rationale: Renders the corridor, particle field and post-processing; roughly half the on-the-wire weight of a full build.

nodes.label: Web Audio API runtime soundtrack
nodes.rationale: The entire soundtrack is synthesised at runtime so there are no audio files to ship; drones are tied to the palette and blips to interaction.

nodes.label: Procedural-only asset policy
nodes.rationale: No video, no 3D model files, no icon fonts, no audio files. Apart from the photographic plates, every visual is CSS, WebGL or Canvas 2D drawn procedurally, which keeps a full build to around 790 kB on the wire — roughly half Three.js and a third the photography.

nodes.label: The photographic plates
nodes.rationale: None of the plates are frames from the series; every plate was rendered for this build in the show's visual language. This keeps the project on the right side of copyright and lets each image be composed for the reveal it must perform — a corridor with headroom for an iris, a break room lit so a lamp-shaped mask finds a table. Plates are never wallpaper: each is a three-layer figure whose reveal, parallax and zoom are animated separately and quoted against the chapter's own timeline.

nodes.label: Image pipeline (node tools/images.mjs)
nodes.rationale: Source art lives in img/src/ and is not served. The tool trims letterbox bars, crops, and emits two WebP widths per plate into img/ plus a generated stylesheet of blur placeholders.

nodes.label: LQIP blur placeholders (plates.lqip.css)
nodes.rationale: Inlined 20-pixel blur placeholders, one per plate, so a chapter shows a colour wash immediately and the full plate a moment later.

nodes.label: Chapter 00 — Induction
nodes.rationale: The Lumon mark resolves out of drifting dust and the title splits into place, using a masked per-character reveal over the WebGL particle field. The atrium plate opens through five gradient bands like blinds and closes the same way to hand over to the lift.

nodes.label: Chapter 01 — The Descent
nodes.rationale: An elevator falls 261 m: doors close, floor counter runs, a waveform crosses the frame, and the entire palette inverts on the exact frame of the severance cut. Built as a scrubbed timeline with an SVG path draw and a mid-scene theme swap. The car stretches vertically with anisotropic scale so the fall smears rather than zooms.

nodes.label: The severance cut (mid-timeline palette inversion)
nodes.rationale: The chapter 01 inversion is the ordinary palette machine fired mid-timeline instead of at a scene boundary — the same mechanism, not a special case, which is why it re-tints DOM, WebGL and audio together.

nodes.label: Chapter 02 — The Floor
nodes.rationale: A dolly down an infinite fluorescent corridor with wing placards sliding past until the MDR door fills the frame. Uses shader-generated corridor geometry and a camera dolly on scroll; an iris opens over the shader corridor and the two hold at matched opacity, one blending into the other.

nodes.label: Chapter 03 — Macrodata Refinement
nodes.rationale: An interactive terminal where clusters that 'feel scary' wobble, resolve and file themselves into a bin as the pointer crosses the number field. Drawn in Canvas 2D with a glyph sprite atlas. The office plate arrives as a letterbox band opening behind the console.

nodes.label: Chapter 04 — Personnel
nodes.rationale: Six dossiers scroll horizontally past a fixed header, each portrait lit by a pointer-following light, using a horizontal pin, halftone gradients and parallax lighting. Four badge photographs surface as each card passes centre; two management dossiers deliberately have no photograph on file.

nodes.label: Chapter 05 — Doctrine
nodes.rationale: Kier's nine tenets rotate through a wheel that detents into place one tenet at a time, driven by a scroll rotation with a dwell curve. Kier's portrait is uncovered top-down by a feathered gradient, like a dust sheet coming off a painting.

nodes.label: Chapter 06 — The Break Room
nodes.rationale: The compliance statement is revealed line by line under a flickering lamp while a deterministic sincerity meter refuses to accept it. The room is masked to the lamp's pool and nothing else, and when the tube stutters the room stutters with it.

nodes.label: Chapter 07 — Egress
nodes.rationale: The particle field reassembles into the Lumon mark via a GPU particle morph to a canvas-sampled target, and a button takes the reader back up. The egress doors rise and push in under the credits, then fade as the mark takes the frame.

nodes.label: One palette, five states (global palette machine)
nodes.rationale: Every colour is a custom property on :root. Scenes declare data-palette, scroll.js watches which scene owns the viewport, and a single data-theme swap on <html> re-tints the DOM, the WebGL scene and the audio mood together over 1.2 s. Centralising colour in one swap is what lets a mid-timeline cut (chapter 01) reuse the same mechanism as a scene boundary.
nodes.norm_label: one palette, five states (global palette machine)

nodes.label: One RAF loop
nodes.rationale: Lenis is driven by gsap.ticker with its own RAF disabled, so smooth scroll, every ScrollTrigger, the cursor springs and the Three.js render all happen in the same frame. Nothing schedules its own loop, which keeps DOM and WebGL from tearing apart.

nodes.label: Transforms have exactly one owner
nodes.rationale: Where a GSAP timeline animates an element's transform, nothing else may touch it. Pointer parallax and magnetic hover instead write CSS custom properties feeding the separate translate property, so the two compose rather than fight.

nodes.label: deviceTier() adaptive quality grading
nodes.rationale: Grades the device from core count, viewport size and (where exposed) device memory, then scales the particle count, the DPR cap and the render resolution accordingly.

nodes.label: Shader-generated corridor
nodes.rationale: The corridor is a handful of large planes whose surface detail — panel seams, ceiling grid, light fittings, floor reflection, fog — is generated entirely in fragment shaders, so an endless hallway costs a few draw calls.

nodes.label: WebGL particle field
nodes.rationale: One Points draw for the whole field; its budget scales with device tier and drops under reduced motion. It carries the dust of the induction and morphs into the Lumon mark at egress.

nodes.label: Single post-processing pass
nodes.rationale: Grain, chromatic aberration, vignette and lens curvature are all carried in one extra pass rather than chained passes.

nodes.label: MDR glyph sprite atlas
nodes.rationale: The MDR grid pre-renders its digits into a sprite atlas once, so a field of ~900 animated cells costs one canvas per frame with no text layout.

nodes.label: No layout reads in scroll handlers
nodes.rationale: Scroll handlers do no layout reads; anything needing measurements takes them in ScrollTrigger's onRefresh, avoiding forced synchronous layout during the scroll frame.
nodes.norm_label: no layout reads in scroll handlers

nodes.label: prefers-reduced-motion handling
nodes.rationale: Turns off scroll smoothing, film grain and scanlines, the camera's idle drift and the lens treatment, and drops the particle budget. Scrubbed timelines stay because they only advance when the reader scrolls — the motion never happens on its own.

nodes.label: Audio gated behind an entry gesture
nodes.rationale: Audio never starts on its own: it waits for the entry gesture in the boot sequence and can be muted from the HUD at any time.
nodes.norm_label: audio gated behind an entry gesture

nodes.label: Custom pointer (fine pointers only)
nodes.rationale: A two-part cursor with contextual labels and magnetic hover, installed only for fine pointers; touch devices keep native behaviour and get tap equivalents for pointer-driven scenes.

nodes.label: Chapters as labelled section landmarks
nodes.rationale: Every chapter is a labelled <section> landmark with a real heading so the narrative can be navigated by region, and the boot screen is dismissable with Enter or Space.

nodes.label: Verification suite (check, smoke, mobile, verify)
nodes.rationale: npm run check parse-checks every module, smoke walks all eight chapters in headless Chrome reporting console errors, mobile repeats at 390×844 with a horizontal-overflow assertion, and verify runs all three.

nodes.label: verify:dist (build then re-walk dist/)
nodes.rationale: The check that matters before a deploy: it proves the minified, bundled, vendored output behaves identically to the source — same document height, same trigger count, same cell count, no console errors.

nodes.label: window.__severance debug handle
nodes.rationale: main.js exposes a debug handle so every headless tool drives the real Lenis instance rather than simulating scroll; all tools also take --dir <folder> to test a build instead of the source.

nodes.label: frame.mjs and probe.mjs inspection probes
nodes.rationale: frame.mjs captures one frame at one scroll position and prints the active palette, which plates are visible at what opacity and decoded size, and the HUD's contrast ratio — useful because a plate that looks fine can still put small type below AA. probe.mjs dumps computed styles and boxes, which is how most of the animation-ownership bugs were found. Both need a local Chrome or Edge since puppeteer-core ships no browser.

nodes.label: Browser support and WebGL fallback
nodes.rationale: Current Chromium, Firefox and Safari; the site leans on color-mix(), svh units, the translate/rotate/scale CSS properties and WebGL 2. Without WebGL the stage is skipped and the DOM narrative plays on its own.

nodes.label: Fan work / no show assets disclaimer
nodes.rationale: Severance is a production of Red Hour / Fifth Season for Apple TV+. No affiliation and no assets from the show: every mark is drawn in code and every photograph was rendered for this build.
nodes.norm_label: fan work / no show assets disclaimer

nodes.label: Atrium Responsive Image Preload
nodes.rationale: The atrium plate is on screen the instant the boot terminal clears, so it is fetched alongside the stylesheets in the head rather than being discovered later by the lazy plate loader. This makes it the LCP candidate and avoids a blank first frame after the preloader.

nodes.label: Persistent Layer Architecture
nodes.rationale: The WebGL canvas, film grain, transition veil, custom pointer and HUD are all placed outside the scroll flow so they survive scene changes and can be driven by a single global timeline instead of being re-created per chapter.

nodes.label: Mid-Scene Palette Switch
nodes.rationale: The descent chapter deliberately carries no data-palette attribute because it owns its palette itself: the outie-to-innie theme flip must land on the exact frame the severance barrier closes, which the generic per-scene palette controller cannot express.

nodes.label: Five-Band Slat Mask Reveal
nodes.rationale: The atrium is revealed through a five-band mask built from a repeating gradient so it opens like blinds and closes the same way when the elevator takes over. The bands are one animated custom property rather than five separate elements, keeping the reveal to a single interpolated value.

nodes.label: Geometry-to-Photography Corridor Handoff
nodes.rationale: The photographic corridor plate is matched to the WebGL corridor's vanishing point and opens as an aperture from frame centre as the rendered hallway dims, so the same space is handed from real-time geometry to a still photograph mid-dolly without a visible cut.

nodes.label: Faceless Management Dossiers
nodes.rationale: Cobel and Milchick carry no photograph on file. This is deliberate rather than a missing asset: the two cards without a face are the two people watching, so the absence itself carries the surveillance reading.

nodes.label: Lamp-Masked Break Room Plate
nodes.rationale: The break room photograph is masked by a radial gradient whose radius is driven by the same flicker timeline as the lamp element, so the room is only visible where the lamp reaches it and the plate and the light source cannot drift out of sync.
